title: Expires must be at least params.minDaysRemaining days in the future

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: It is RECOMMENDED that the value of this field be less than a year into the future to avoid staleness.
spec.note: conformance_testable is false because RFC 9116 imposes no minimum-days-remaining threshold -- see policy_note. normative_quote is now the verbatim RECOMMENDED sentence of §2.5.5, transcribed from the immutable rfc9116.txt on 2026-07-30 (identical to the sentence already verified in security-txt-expires-missing). The 30-day floor this rule actually enforces is local operational policy (params.minDaysRemaining), recorded in policy_note, not implied by the quote.

policy_note: RFC 9116 §2.5.5 requires only that Expires be future-dated (see security-txt-expired) and RECOMMENDS under one year (OQ5, deferred to the first ratchet increment). The 30-day floor here is a LOCAL operational buffer so the monthly audit cadence (audit-web.yml monthly job) gets at least one warning cycle before the file actually expires. It is supplied by params.minDaysRemaining and read by check-security-txt.mjs on the production path (main()'s call to validateSecurityTxt) -- it is not restated as a separate literal in the validator. RFC 9116 places no lower bound on how far out Expires must be, and does not require a warning window before expiry; the 30-day floor is entirely this repo's operational choice (its prior home in normative_quote as commentary was moved here in the ADR 0011 follow-up (a) review pass).
applicability: A security.txt body containing a parseable, non-past Expires value.
expectation: The parsed Expires instant is at least params.minDaysRemaining days after the evaluation instant.

cases.name: exactly at the threshold passes -- the comparison is strict (<), not (<=)
40 days out -- probe C perturbs params.minDaysRemaining past this to prove it is the real comparison operand
no Expires field -- this rule is inapplicable, security-txt-expires-missing (and security-txt-contact-missing) fire instead
